description: Generates a Euclidean rhythm and a melody drawn from a chosen mode and melodic pattern, with a monophonic pitch output and a polyphonic chord output

params.text: Sets the rate of the module's own clock, marked in BPM, 60 BPM in its default position and doubling for each unit of the knob's travel
Advances the pattern by one step each time it is pressed, whether the clock input is patched or not; the maker's manual calls this a light rather than a button
Starts and stops the pattern; the module comes up running
Returns the pattern to its first step and rebuilds the melody
Scales the voltage at the tempo input before it is added to the tempo knob, from nothing at the counter-clockwise end to the whole voltage at the clockwise end
Sets the root note, in semitones over one octave
Chooses the mode, drawn from the major, harmonic minor, melodic minor, harmonic major and double harmonic major scales
Chooses the melodic pattern, which sets the order the degrees of the scale are played in; 1357F walks the first, third, fifth and seventh degrees forwards, and RANDOM picks freely from the scale
Shifts the pitch outputs two octaves down to two octaves up
Scales the voltage at the root CV input before it multiplies the root knob
Scales the voltage at the scale CV input before it multiplies the scale knob
Scales the voltage at the pattern CV input before it multiplies the pattern knob, despite the maker's tooltip naming it Division CV
Scales the voltage at the octave CV input before it multiplies the octave knob
Sets the number of steps in the cycle, one to thirty-six; a melodic pattern longer than this is cut short
Rotates the melodic pattern, so that with the pattern 1357F and a rotation of one the cycle begins on the third degree
Sets how many notes the chord output carries, from a triad up to an eleventh chord
Scales the voltage at the chord CV input before it multiplies the chord knob
Sets how many of the steps carry a hit, which the module spreads over the cycle as a Euclidean pattern
Scales the voltage at the rotate CV input before it multiplies the rotate knob
Scales the voltage at the steps CV input before it multiplies the steps knob, despite the maker's tooltip naming it Size CV
Scales the voltage at the density CV input before it multiplies the density knob

inputs.text: Added to the tempo knob after the trimmer beside it, one volt doubling the rate; it changes nothing while a cable is in the clock input
Advances the pattern one step on each rising edge above 2V; with nothing patched here the module runs from its own clock at the rate the tempo knob sets
A rising edge above 2V starts the pattern, and the next one stops it
A rising edge above 2V returns the pattern to its first step and rebuilds the melody
Multiplies the root knob by this voltage, scaled by the trimmer beside it; with the knob at zero the voltage sets the root on its own
Multiplies the scale knob by this voltage, scaled by the trimmer beside it, so a cable resting at 0V holds the first mode
Multiplies the pattern knob by this voltage, scaled by the trimmer beside it, so a cable resting at 0V holds the first melodic pattern
Multiplies the octave knob by this voltage, scaled by the trimmer beside it; with the knob at zero the voltage sets the octave on its own
Multiplies the rotate knob by this voltage, scaled by the trimmer beside it, so a cable resting at 0V leaves the pattern unrotated
Multiplies the chord knob by this voltage, scaled by the trimmer beside it, so a cable resting at 0V leaves the chord at a triad
Multiplies the steps knob by this voltage, scaled by the trimmer beside it; the result is held at one step or more
Multiplies the density knob by this voltage, scaled by the trimmer beside it, so a cable resting at 0V leaves no hits in the cycle

outputs.text: 10V through a step that carries a hit, and 0V through the steps that do not
A 1ms pulse at 10V on each step that carries a hit
The pitch of the current step, one note at a time, at 1V per octave
The chord built on the current step, one note per channel, with one channel for each note the chord knob sets
A 1ms pulse at 10V when the cycle returns to its first step

notes: the eight CV inputs multiply their knobs rather than adding to them, so a cable resting at 0V pulls the control to its lowest value and the knob does nothing while that cable is in
the black bar across the panel reads out the knob values rather than the notes being played
a small knob is drawn over the eoc jack and takes the click, so dragging there turns the tempo CV trimmer instead of starting a cable
